All India raw coal production during 2023-24 reached 997.83 million tonnes, compared with 893.19 million tonnes in 2022-23, a growth of 11.71 per cent. Coal India Limited contributed 773.81 million tonnes. The increase was driven by higher output from the large opencast mines of SECL and MCL, faster clearances for mine expansion, improved evacuation through first mile connectivity projects, and higher mechanisation with surface miners.
Table 3.1: Subsidiary-wise raw coal production of CIL (in Million Tonnes)
Table 3.2: Company-wise raw coal production, All India (in Million Tonnes)

Raw coal offtake by CIL during 2023-24 was 753.50 million tonnes against 694.70 million tonnes in 2022-23. Supply to the power sector accounted for about 80 per cent of the offtake. Coal stocks at pitheads remained comfortable through the year owing to improved rake availability.

explain.question: Why was offtake affected by rake availability?

notes: no entity named — showing All India / CIL
no year named — using latest available (FY2023-24)

explain.answer: The evidence indicates that improved rake availability led to comfortable coal stocks at pitheads, which in turn likely contributed to increased offtake. This is supported by the statement that "coal stocks at pitheads remained comfortable through the year owing to improved rake availability" [2]. The improved rake availability would have allowed for more efficient coal handling and potentially higher offtake rates. However, the exact mechanism by which rake availability affected offtake is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence.

parts.question: the steps taken to improve evacuation?
parts.answer: The steps taken to improve evacuation include expediting environment and forest clearances, capacity expansion of existing mines, and improving evacuation through first mile connectivity [9]. The government has also attributed growth to faster statutory clearances, digital monitoring of mines, and the commissioning of new first mile connectivity projects [10]. These measures aim to enhance production and ensure efficient mine expansion.

reports.title: Subsidiary-wise Coal Production and Offtake — FY2023-24

sections.text: In FY2023-24, Coal India Limited recorded coal production of 773.80 MT [18], +10.04% against FY2022-23. Among the subsidiaries, MCL was the largest at 207.10 MT [14] (26.8% of the total) and NEC the smallest at 0.20 MT [16].

In FY2023-24, Coal India Limited recorded coal offtake / despatch of 753.50 MT [36], +8.46% against FY2022-23. Among the subsidiaries, MCL was the largest at 206.40 MT [32] (27.4% of the total) and NEC the smallest at 0.20 MT [34].

Chapter 3: Production
All India raw coal production during 2023-24 reached 997.83 million tonnes, compared with 893.19 million tonnes in 2022-23, a growth of 11.71 per cent. Coal India Limited contributed 773.81 million tonnes. The increase was driven by higher output from the large opencast mines of SECL and MCL, faster clearances for mine expansion, improved evacuation through first mile connect
